title: IGR_U985_RNASeq
description: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), the most frequent adult leukemia in western countries, is a clonal accumulation of mature B-lymphocytes and its natural history is yet unclear. By using sequencing and cellular biology approaches on a cohort of CLL patient samples, we show here that acquired CLL mutations are observed in hematopoietic multipotent progenitor fractions in the majority of patients. These early CLL mutations include recurrent inactivating mutations in NFKBIE (10.7%) and missense mutations in BRAF (3.6%) and EGR2 (8.3%). Functional analyses demonstrated that BRAF-G469R affects lymphoid differentiation and transforms the T-cell lineage in vivo. In addition, the EGR2 recurrent mutations were associated with transcriptional activation of EGR2 target genes in patients and cell cycle abnormality in cellular model. Our findings indicate that CLL may develop from an initial infra-clinic, pre-leukemic phase affecting immature hematopoietic cells. We perform RNA-seq experiments on three EGR2-E356K samples, one EGR2-H384N sample and seven EGR2 wildtype patients. The RNA was extracted from B cells. The cDNA libraries were prepared using the ScriptSeq Complete Kit (Epicentre) and we performed paired-end sequencing (100 bp) using HiSeq2000 sequencing instruments.

samples.title: CLL040_2
samples.description: Protocols: The source material was bone marrow or blood cells from Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) patients. Mononuclear cells (MNC) are separated through a density gradient (Ficoll). From MNC, B cells are FACS sorted using the CD19 marker. CD19+ cells were pellet after sorting and the RNA was extracted.
